result.process_description:
Consider a process for purchasing items from an online shop.
The user starts an order by logging in to their account.
Then, the user simultaneously selects the items to purchase and sets a payment method.
Afterward, the user either pays or completes an installment agreement.
After selecting the items, the user chooses between multiple options for a free reward.
Since the reward value depends on the purchase value, this step is done after selecting the items, but it is independent of the payment activities.
Finally, the items are delivered.
The user has the right to return items for exchange.
Every time items are returned, a new delivery is made.

result.rule: Several unconditional outgoing flows from one activity can all proceed. Use a gateway when the description requires a decision or synchronization.
Distinguish message tasks from message events: a task models performed work; an event models a message occurrence affecting flow.
An ordinary embedded subprocess participates in normal sequence flow and may contain its own starts, ends, activities, gateways and flows.
Allow multiple start or end events when the description has distinct triggers or outcomes. Do not force all outcomes into one end.
Use a parallel split when all outgoing branches start. Do not add decision conditions to parallel branches.

Give every process and every expanded subProcess its own explicit start event and end event. A trigger that occurs after the main flow (for example later feedback or a return) is joined to the main flow by a gateway, or modeled as an event subprocess or a separate process.

result.rule: When the description states that one activity is followed by two or more separate actions that all must happen, with no order stated between them, and the process continues only after all of them are done: Model a parallel gateway that splits the flow after the preceding activity into one branch per action, with each action as its own task. Close the branches with a parallel gateway before the next activity that needs all of them. Also place a parallel gateway around any activity the description lists as a separate, unordered step within such a group, so that each stated step keeps its own position in the flow. Do not use an exclusive gateway for branches that must all complete.

When the description states that a step follows one earlier activity, is independent of the payment-related branches that run alongside it, and the process continues only after all of these parallel steps are done: Start the independent step from the same parallel (AND) split that opens the simultaneous branches, with its own unconditional outgoing flow and its own task. Do not route that branch through another parallel gateway in series, and do not let it pass through a gateway that belongs to another branch. Close all branches with one parallel join before the next decision or step that waits on them, and connect each branch's final task to that join.

When the description lists several distinct actions that all follow one point, joined by commas and 'and', with no order stated between them (for example, 'X, Y, and Z' after an event): Model each listed action as its own task. Place a parallel (AND) split after the common point so that all branches start, and join them with a parallel gateway before the shared continuation. Do not add decision conditions to these branches and do not serialize them in an arbitrary order.

When the description lists several activities that follow the same point with no stated order between them, and the following step waits until all of them are finished: Model each such activity as a parallel branch. Route the incoming flow from the preceding point into a parallel gateway that fans out with one unconditional outgoing flow to each listed activity. Route each activity's outgoing flow into a second parallel gateway that joins the branches before the next step. Do not connect the preceding point to only one of the activities, and do not use an exclusive gateway for branches that must all be finished.
